title: Basic Checkmate Patterns: Back-Rank Mate
summary: A classic pattern: trap the king on its own back rank.

steps.text: The BACK-RANK MATE is a classic pattern: if a king is stuck on its home rank with its own pawns blocking every escape square, a rook or queen can swoop down the open file and checkmate it! Look how the pawns on f7, g7, and h7 actually trap their own king here.

steps.prompt: Find the move that traps Black's king with a back-rank checkmate!
steps.successText: Checkmate! The rook owns the whole back rank.
steps.retryText: Slide your rook all the way up the open file to the back rank.

steps.prompt: Queens can deliver back-rank mate too! Slide her all the way to h8.
steps.successText: Checkmate — queens are just as deadly on the back rank!
steps.retryText: Slide your queen all the way up the open file to the back rank.

steps.text: The defense against back-rank mate is simple: always leave your king a little breathing room — like moving a pawn on the g-file or h-file — so he has an escape square if needed.
Next: let's learn how to checkmate with a king and queen against a lone king.
